text_fidelity_a:
Poly - Voyager Focus 2 UC USB-C Headset (Plantronics) - Bluetooth Dual-Ear (Stereo) Headset with Boom Mic - USB-C PC/Mac Compatible - Active Noise Canceling - Works with Teams, Zoom (Certified) & More Ok, so I have to admit at first I was wondering why someone would spend this much on a Bluetooth headset that isn't a feature-rich entertainment one like those from Sony or a major fad brand like Beats, both of which I have some experience with. But this, no... this is actually something different. This is a serious tool for serious use with serious built quality and seriously useful features. Seriously.
For example, the telescoping mouthpiece means you'll get unparalleled mic quality compared to headsets that pick the mic up by your ears (looking at YOU, airpods!), both in clarity and isolation from background noise. You can also physically bend it out of the way, or use the button on the mic itself to mute. Try doing that with airpods. Then there's the button based features. Shortcuts and touch-sensitive buttons are cool on aesthetic devices, but the physical controls on this are an ergonomic user experience DREAM. Everything is easy to access and control, no apps or press-and-hold or counting LED blinks, etc. Sort of makes me miss the old days of phones with physical switches and buttons. When you want your equipment to get serious, this is the sort of user experience you expect. Then there's the charging rack. OMG I love that, I can store it on my desk and it's charging automagically. Pick it up and put it on, ready to go. Never needs to be charged because it's been charging in between uses. Finally, I'm really impressed with the USB dongle option. You see, the one thing I really dislike about wireless headphones is that you usually need to pair it with a device, then unpair it to switch to another device. For example, using my Sony headphones on my phone and tablet, if my wife wants to borrow them for a zoom meeting, I need to pair with her device but then also unpair with mine so that it doesn't keep trying to reconnect to it. Sometimes we just give up and use a wired headset to avoid that mess. Non-bluetooth wireless headsets have a dongle, which makes it easy to swap what you are connected to (no unpairing needed, just move the dongle) but then you can't connect to devices without a USB port like a phone. This is the best of both- you can pair it with your phone, but ALSO use the USB to quickly connect with your desktop or laptop without going through the process of pairing and unpairing. This is the kind of usability and professional quality I would expect from a brand like Plantronics, and all the while it works well as a stereo headset for music/gaming/etc as well. Very comfortable to wear for long hours, I'd highly recommend it for serious users.
text_fidelity_b: Poly - Voyager Focus 2 UC USB-C Headset (Plantronics) - Bluetooth Dual-Ear (Stereo) Headset with Boom Mic - USB-C PC/Mac Compatible - Active Noise Canceling - Works with Teams, Zoom (Certified) & More

text_fidelity_a:
Apple Watch Series 7 [GPS + Cellular 45mm] Smart Watch w/Graphite Stainless Steel Case with Midnight Sport Band. Fitness Tracker, Blood Oxygen & ECG Apps, Always-On Retina Display, Water Resistant This is my fourth Apple watch. I’ve purchased the series 0, series 1, 2, two series 4. One stainless, one aluminum. The 4 is such a great watch, I never felt the need to upgrade. I recently paid Apple $ 79 to replace my battery. They actually replaced the watch. I’ve never had a problem with any Apple watch. I purchased the 7, because of a great Amazon price.

Stainless steel vs aluminum. Both are great. I put one bad scratch on my aluminum crystal. It doesn’t affect function, and it only shows when the watch is dark. It happened when my watch hit the rough edge of our granite countertop. My SS has never scratched.

Why spend the extra money to get the stainless? If you want a GPS only model, the SS is $ 300 more than the aluminum. If you want cellular capability, the difference drops to $ 200. Due to health issues, my wife convinced me to get the cellular capability. In an emergency, these will call 911, even when your phone is not around, and even when you don’t subscribe for service. That’s important.

The series 7 has a blood oxygen measurement feature. During Covid, we purchased two different fingertip devices to measure blood oxygen. We were disappointed with both. The watch oxygen measurement works seamlessly. We consider it worth buying for that feature alone.

Summary.

If you want cellular capability, spend the extra $ 200 for SS. If you don’t, buy the aluminum model and save $ 300.
Both are great watches.
text_fidelity_b: Apple Watch Series 7 [GPS + Cellular 45mm] Smart Watch w/Graphite Stainless Steel Case with Midnight Sport Band. Fitness Tracker, Blood Oxygen & ECG Apps, Always-On Retina Display, Water Resistant

text_fidelity_a:
Sony MDREX38iP/BLK EX Earbud with iPod Remote Control - Black For moderate priced earbuds, these are pretty good. The sound quality is much better than average, with smooth response across the range. The highs are detailed, and not shrill. The midbass is clear, with no unnatural peak that sometimes passes for "bass boost". The deep bass is natural, and not artificially strong. Very easy to listen to for extended sessions.

For comfort, these are pretty average -- not the best comfort, but not bad either. There are interchangeable ear tips you can try out for the best fit. There's a lot of personal preference as to what's going to stay in the ear comfortably. The earbuds are angled, so you have to pay attention to the left/right orientation.

This is advertised as "iPhone compatible", meaning that there's a mic with tiny + and - buttons attached to the left ear piece. I'm a BlackBerry guy, and I'm happy to report that the mic works fine with my BlackBerry Bold 9700. But the + and - buttons don't have any effect (they don't raise or lower the volume). However, pressing the small button between the + and - buttons will either pause the song that's playing, or mute a phone call. Pretty handy.

Sound isolation is not a strong point of this set. I wasn't sure what to expect, so I guess I'm not disappointed. Probably you'd want to look elsewhere if sound isolation is important to you.

Durability may also be an issue. The wire is very thin, and it feels fragile, especially where it connects to the earbud. I'll know in 6 to 12 months whether these will stand up to regular use. The 90-degree plug will take wear better for many people, depending on how it connects to your phone, MP3 player or computer. Comes with a little storage pouch, which is good protection for the set when not in use.
text_fidelity_b: Sony MDREX38iP/BLK EX Earbud with iPod Remote Control - Black

text_fidelity_a: Echo Dot (2nd Generation) - Smart speaker with Alexa - White So... I own both the tower and now several dots.  Of course the dots are more reasonably priced, however, the speaker ability is really where it's vastly different.  Obviously the tower is much better in the speaker department.  However, I did find that there is a cordless speaker you can buy to go with your 2nd gen dot that is an improvement and still at lower price point than the tower when combined with the cost of the dot. (Mokcao cordless speaker - amazon sells it too) Because the dots are so reasonably priced we have them in all 3 major rooms and use the cordless speaker to drop one dot in and take it outside to our sunroom when we like.  Over all, I am pleased with both my tower AND dots... but probably will stick to dot purchases in the future because of the price point.  I would say if you've been on the fence, the dot is well worth a try.  It's very easy to set up, you will need to download the app, also easy to follow step by step setups.  Once you're hooked up you will be amazed at how often you use Alexa.  At our house she helps me keep track of where I am supposed to be every day... timers... night time meditation... the occasional argument and even plays games with us as well as much needed comedic relief.  It may not be "necessary" to have Alexa, but I am always surprised at how often we use her assistance.  It's nice and worth it to us.  I never hesitate to update my reviews should new info seem useful.

Samsung UN46EH6000 46-Inch 1080p 120Hz LED HDTV (Black) (2012 Model) This TV ROCKS. After reading the other reviews before purchasing, I was aware that some modification of the base settings were required. Menu is intuitive and easy to navigate. The remote is very nice, I love the fact that you can backlight the remote buttons if your like me and don't memorize the key layout on the remote. One heck of a upgrade from a 32 inch CRT based TV! Some of the reviews mentioned that the sound quality could be at issue but after a couple of days of wearing in the sound has gotten to the point where I am rarely going over 30 on the sound. It's not a smart TV but that wasn't a concern for me anyway.

Update July 2015, This TV has started acting up, I will be calling the 1-800-samsung and see what they say but with looking at the information on the web, it seems as if this tv is experiencing the same problems that their older TV's had which is power supply issues. It won't turn on sometimes, or it will take 30 seconds to power up, or other variations. I wish that I had known about these issues before I purchased this TV because I might have looked at different manufacturers..

Called the 800 number found out that manufacturer warranty is gone obviously. No offers of a free diagnostic or anything like that. MEE audio Atlas Sky IML Graphics On-Ear Headphones with Headset Functionality [[VIDEOID:98df0cfb6b0daad3ff2eecda806c4550]] Without a doubt, these are the most beautiful headphones made today, and I suspect that while others may follow, I doubt they will come even slightly close to this stunning set.
A few years ago, HP introduced the Vivienne Tam Mini, a red floral netbook with a matching scarf and bag. The following year was a gold butterfly version, seen in the Sex in the City film.
These machines were ridiculously expensive for the specs, but you paid for the designer and design, not printed on the case, but using a process known as in-mold labeling.
They were beyond gorgeous.

When I saw these, I knew right away that it was in-mold labeling, and someone finally embraced what the 'big guys' have been slow to catch up on.
There are those of us that want a DESIGN, not just a color, that speaks to us when we choose things that are personal to us, like headphones. We don't always want it to be the version selected by the celeb du jour, either.

I also knew I HAD to have a set! It was a tough call between the clean throwback lines of the Tron-esque 'Orion' and the opposite celestial dreaming of 'Skyline', the later being the winner by a nose (ear?).

WOW! Visually, you simply can not get better. You'll want to wear them everywhere, and here is the best part, you CAN. Unlike noise-cancelling headphones, you can still hear a bit of what's going on around you. I can finally get great sound and not worry that I'm missing the doorbell/dog bark/police siren or whatever.

They are light, in a comfortable way, not a cheap way. They fit over the ear as opposed to surrounding it, so you will not get a strong bass unless you fit the band slide perfectly. Since it adjusts smoothly, no problem.
You also don't wind up looking like you're wearing a Princess Leia wig...the big donuts over each ear.

Not many of us can carry that off, right?

But back to the sound...after all, it's what's UNDER the hood that counts.
Be it my iPhone, iPad, Galaxy (phone & tablet), PC, or Mac (tech household, what can I say), the sound is consistently true. Unlike some headphones tuned to over-accentuate bass, these nail it perfectly. That means classical comes through as beautifully as techno. And speedcore/splittercore comes through as.....well, speedcore/splittercore!

Buy for the looks, keep them for your ears and brain.
text_fidelity_b: MEE audio Atlas Sky IML Graphics On-Ear Headphones with Headset Functionality

Belkin 8-Outlet Surge Protector with Power Cord Organizer, Designed for Office and Conference Room I have a huge Belkin surge protector in my office that meets all of my needs and also occasionally makes me lunch (it's pretty rad), but since having a baby, I've found that my definition of "rad" has changed to mean not visible, attractive, or accessible by the baby. While this isn't meant to be babyproof, I've found that the cage-like design and locking mechanism not only keep my cords tidier, but also makes them a lot less obvious and exciting to baby so that when it is placed out of reach, he isn't always clamoring to be lifted up to it, as he does with high-up cords that are not as hidden.

Two things that I don't love: One is that the sliding mechanism that opens out to allow you to put the cords in and use the diagonally-sliding plugs easily - they are a little stiff. So stiff that in fact I doubted whether I was really supposed to slide them out and was afraid I'd break the thing. I also found the locking/ opening/ closing mechanism too stiff - in fact, I gashed my finger when it opened unexpectedly after having to push it harder than I should have to open it.

The other thing is that there is no method for hanging this outlet on the wall. So I have to set it on a high shelf, which is less cool than just hanging it behind my printer or something.

Otherwise, I love that I can neaten up a decidedly un-neat portion of my office with this, and be assured of clean power to boot.
text_fidelity_b: Belkin 8-Outlet Surge Protector with Power Cord Organizer, Designed for Office and Conference Room

Fast forward, I am cleaning out a drawer and found the drive again. I remembered it had issues but my spider senses said plug it into the USB on the Xbox 360 and it worked. MavisLink HDMI Cable Fiber Optic 100ft 4K 60Hz HDMI2.0b 18Gbps HDR10 ARC HDCP2.2 YUV4:4:4/4:2:2/4:2:0 Slim Flexible for HDTV/Game Console/Projector/Home Theatre I gave this a four because it did not work on one out of three devices I tried it with (and I know each to work with a short HDMI cable). I'm not sure why this had a lot of flickering when used with my Alienware computer, but it worked perfectly with another computer and my QNAP NAS (worth noting is the NAS puts out a very weak signal and does not work with my in-place 25-ft. traditional HDMI cable).

I had almost written this off because usually HDMI is a crapshoot when it comes to any sort of distance and I didn't even realize such a product existed until I read about fiber optic cable inside. I thought that was a generic brand typo type of situation until I looked this up and realized this is a real thing. I didn't study it, but I gather/assume that there is a chip inside that changes electrical signals to low power lasers to send the signals this way. Interesting, though, because there are not 19 fibers inside (a traditional HDMI cable has 19 pins, I think).

I probably need to research this further just because it's totally cool, but I love this thing because I can now watch my NAS directly on my TV even though it is down in the basement (and there is a great app to act as a remote since I now do not have line of sight for the IR remote). I only took off a star because it apparently has some issues with my one computer - not sure why but if you need a couple of these, you might want to buy one at a time to be sure what it does and does not work with. I love it, but had to remove a star for that reason.
text_fidelity_b: MavisLink HDMI Cable Fiber Optic 100ft 4K 60Hz HDMI2.0b 18Gbps HDR10 ARC HDCP2.2 YUV4:4:4/4:2:2/4:2:0 Slim Flexible for HDTV/Game Console/Projector/Home Theatre

LotFancy Laptop Cooler Cooling Pad with 5 Quiet Fans for 12-17" Notebook, Dual USB Ports A good laptop chiller pad becomes important when you run a lot of graphics-intensive games or if you are doing anything requiring the CPU to run a heavy load. Heat is the enemy of a computer system and the fastest way to a dead laptop is to not deal with heat issues when there’s a problem. I had a chill pad some time ago and it was sub-par. This one by LotFancy is much better and it does a good job.

First off, this is a big chill pad, the same basic dimensions as my laptop but much thicker. I have a 15.6" laptop and this pad is almost a perfect and exact fit, with only a narrow area in the back that extends past the end of the laptop. If you want a small and petite chill pad, this is not the one you want. It does incline too with a metal bar and slots in the case so that the laptop can be angled up. This actually is good for exposing it to even more air.

This chill pad connects to a USB port so it can either be plugged into a port on the computer or into a hub. There are two ports on it and both seem to be the same in terms of how the pad operates. That is, the pad operates at the same speed regardless of which port is used. There are also two buttons on the pad for turning it on. One turns on the larger fan in the middle, and the other turns on all the other fans. Two green LEDs next to those buttons indicate that the pad is powered on and working.

This pad moves a lot of air and it does a good job of cooling the laptop. But, it does so very quietly which is a huge plus. I have it set up in my home office and the pad makes about as much noise as a desktop computer, maybe a little less. The sound it makes is a gentle hum.

When powered on each fan has a bright blue LED in it. While they look cool when there’s no laptop on the pad, they’re all but invisible when the laptop is sitting on top. There isn’t even much of a glow coming from the pad. I turned on the pad, turned out all of the lights and the glow from the laptop screen was enough to overpower any light that might have come from the pad. Except for the low hum I wouldn’t know it was even turned on.

This is a good chill pad. It works quietly and it moves a lot of air. Compared to other chill pads I have used this one is very good and I am happy to recommend it.

Disclaimer: I was provided a sample of this product in exchange for a fair, honest and thorough review. Even though I received this product at no cost I have rated and reviewed this product without bias, based solely on my experience with it.
text_fidelity_b: LotFancy Laptop Cooler Cooling Pad with 5 Quiet Fans for 12-17" Notebook, Dual USB Ports

TiVo Roamio 500 GB DVR (Old Version) - Digital Video Recorder and Streaming Media Player Update. April 12, 2014. 4 months after purchase.

I have unplugged the TIVO, will pay the monthly fees for the next 8 months. At least I'll save the $ 3 month cable card fees.

I got another tuner. The tuner works. I have 2 TIVOs and the new tuner works in the old TIVO, but not the new Roamio. It is a Roamio problem.
I now only get 4 standard def stations with the Roamio.

TIVO offered to replace the Roamio for a flat $ 49, plus shipping. I figure the total cost will be $ 75. I'm sure I will get a refurbished TIVO.
Decided it wasn't worth spending $ 75 to get a refurbished TIVO, which may or may not work. Since my ROKU 3 gives me Time Warner Demand channels, it is much less compelling to have a TIVO.

I'll keep the TIVO Premiere connected as it has a lifetime and is trouble free, The Time Warner demand capability of the ROKU 3 is a major threat to TIVO's existence.

I did purchase the TIVO on Amazon with the AMEX credit card which doubles the warranty. I called AMEX. Was told it would not cover the cost of the replacement ($ 49). Only would cover the labor cost, since parts were still under the TIVO warranty (90 days labor, 1 year parts). Since labor isn't separately charged, I'm not covered. Think that stinks.

Update. 105 days later.

Well warranty is up by 15 days. TIVO doesn't recognize tuning adapter. My old premiere works perfectly.
Time Warner spent 2 hours at my home today, swapped out cable cards and tried 3 different tuning adapters. It's a TIVO issue.
I bypassed tuning adapter for a direct hookup. Gives me half the channels. When my one year committment is up, I'll scrap it.

Only saving grace. When I called to cancel my 13 month old Premier XL, they offered me a lifetime for $ 199. I took it.
Do not recommend it Roamio. I was one of the original TIVO users. A 45 hour standard definition TIVO. Very disappointed.

Original review.

Integrated Wi Fi. It's about time. This is my 4th TIVO. Currently paying for 2 monthly subscriptions. Have been satisfied with all my TIVOs. Getting rid of the $ 90 Wi Fi accessory is a big plus. Our other TIVO is a 2 tuner Premiere XL that holds 300 hours of HD. We've never had it over 25% , so 75 hours is enough for us. Our other TIVO has been moved to the bedroom. We really needed at least a 4 tuner set. Two tuners may seem enough, but the stations are now playing it cute by ending programs at 9:01 instead of 9. This causes a conflict and forces you to cancel a show, or not watch a live station at the same time. It effectively reduces the two tuner to a one tuner. Before your TIVO arrives, go to your cable source (if you use cable), and get the appropriate cable card for a 4 tuner set, and tuning adapter. TW charges me $ 2.80 each for the cards. One for each TV. You need to call your cable company to activate and pair your cable card. TW has a great system, and it took only minutes to do. You also need to have an HDMI cable on hand, and a USB to HDMI cable. The kind that connects from your wired printer to your computer.

I also pay monthly, not lifetime. On my original TIVO, an old 45 hour SD job, I took a $ 199 lifetime plan after 2 months. Three weeks later, a nearby lightning strike wiped out the modem on my TIVO, and my computer. Yes, I did have surge protectors, as well as a $ 300 whole house surge protector sold and installed by my electric company. End of my TIVO, end of my $ 199 lifetime plan. TIVO offered no sympathy. So TIVO yes. Lifetime plan NO.

You cannot stream to your mobile devices with the 4 tuner TIVO, without adding accessories.

Added. You also need a short coaxial cable. My prior TIVO packages included every possible cable you may need. No longer. The power supply, remote, remote batteries, and the TIVO were all that were included. An added explanation on the usb needed. The standard side of the USB connection connects to the TIVO. The printer type side connects to the tuning adapter. I went to my junk box, and pulled an old printer cable out. It's not the older type with the large ends. It is a very small odd sided type that plugs in. The cable company should be providing these. Ask them for one.
text_fidelity_b: TiVo Roamio 500 GB DVR (Old Version) - Digital Video Recorder and Streaming Media Player

My cell phone found it in seconds, and in less than a minute I was listening to music from my cell phone, only out of this little speaker, it actually sounded great. Fire Tablet with Alexa, 7" Display, 16 GB, Blue - with Special Offers (Previous Generation - 5th) I've had my Kindle for about 6 months and I am more excited about it now than when I bought it. Adapting to the format and operation was a snap. Pros >> Cons.

Pros: I can take more books than I could possibly carry with me on vacation. The charger is good for 110-240V so I can easily recharge it, with an appropriate plug adaptor, anywhere I go. I can browse the bookstore from home and request samples to read that download to my kindle in a few seconds. I even found, sampled, and bought a book while traveling on the DC Metro. Approximately 75% of the books I'm interested in reading can be purchased in the Kindle format. I have found, read, and enjoyed books I normally would not have tried because of the ability to sample a fair amount of text before purchasing them. I am reading more e-books than I did paper books.

Cons: It is frustrating not to be able to share a good book with a friend. I wish I could organize the content into folders and sub-folders on the display instead of just having a single level directory that goes on for pages. I tried a newspaper subscription but the e-delivery was spotty and often delayed and I really didn't enjoy reading the content that way. I am spending much more money on e-books than I spent on paper books because I am buying/reading more.
text_fidelity_b: Fire Tablet with Alexa, 7" Display, 16 GB, Blue - with Special Offers (Previous Generation - 5th)

text_fidelity_a:
Samsung T3 Portable SSD - 2TB - USB 3.1 External SSD (MU-PT2T0B/AM) I like tech. I've had a computer since the commodore Vic-20 came out. That being said I'm not into competing with or against other computers and computer users. I don't run testing or speed diagnostics on my hardware. If it works and feels or seems to be working as advertised and expected I'm completely happy. I just don't care to sit here are see how many micro-seconds faster my new drive is than my older ones.
All that being said I use external drives exclusively for maintaining backups of my personal files, photos, documents, music, eBooks, Etc. Everything else I can simply reinstall in a couple hours. I don't have that many things installed. My computing needs are simple. But I have lost files due to a drive crash so I meticulously make weekly backups of my important files. Currently I've been using two USB 3.0 Seagate Backup Plus drives to make my backups every Monday.
This new Samsung solid state drive is remarkably faster at copying files to than my mechanical drives and easily a quarter the size and weight of the Seagate drives. I had a couple hiccups when I first formatted the drive to NTFS (I had no need of proprietary encryption) and started copying my files over to the drive but after one or two false starts I got tens of thousands of files copied over with no more problems and have for several weeks just copied new files to the existing collections in their directories and once again this SSD drive flies through the process much faster than the Seagate drives. Now I have three complete backups of my files and feel that much safer and secure with three copies of my files and I love that there's no moving parts. The cable's long enough, about eighteen inches, to work fine with my laptop though someone with a desktop may want to invest in a longer cable.
I'm knocking one star off for a device this expensive not coming with even a cheap hard shell case or even a rubber plug to protect the USB port from dust. It's the one point of possible entry of foreign matter into the drive and causing damage or failure. For the price they're currently charging it wouldn't have been any real hardship to include a case or plug to protect this device.
text_fidelity_b: Samsung T3 Portable SSD - 2TB - USB 3.1 External SSD (MU-PT2T0B/AM)

text_fidelity_a:
Lenovo IdeaCentre 3 Desktop Tower, AMD Athlon Silver 3050U, AMD Radeon Graphics, 4GB DDR4, 256GB SSD, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, HDMI, Windows 10 You may know about the announcement from Lenovo a few weeks ago that going forward the company will be certifying all their ThinkPad and Thinkstation workstations for Linux. This computer is an IdeaCentre, not a ThinkPad or ThinkStation, and it comes preloaded with Windows, but I am a Linux user and I wanted to see if it will run Linux.

First things first: If you're looking for a gaming computer or something to handle graphics-intensive programs, this isn't it. It doesn't have a screaming fast processor, although it is a capable one. The onboard AMD Raven graphics module is pretty capable (I tried it out on a big display), but this model has no expansion slot for a video or audio card or any other such upgrades.

It does have a bay for a big 3.5 inch HDD with SATA connectors. And it comes with a 256GB SSD already installed on the motherboard. It also comes with 4GB RAM (and a second slot to add more), and a wired keyboard and mouse and the power supply. It has four USB 2.0 ports in the back, and two 2.0 and two 3.0 (gen 1) USB ports in the front. Also on the front are a card reader slot, the optical drive, mic and headset connection ports, and the power button. The back also has an HDMI port, VGA-out port, and and ethernet port.

It's about the size of an ITX mini tower form factor box, which is a little larger than a big dictionary. It stands upright, so the footprint is pretty small. And it's lightweight compared to a big desktop box.

I didn't even complete the first boot into Windows before attempting a Linux install. Tapping F2 on boot will get you into a graphical menu for picking your boot device, and F12 will get you into a deeper menu for selecting boot order and into the BIOS.

My favorite distro is Debian, so I thought I'd take a shot at installing it. It was a no-go. It didn't have the drivers for the onboard Atheros wifi card, and apparently a few other things. I actually pulled the wifi card off the motherboard and substituted a dongle and gave it a second try. I got Debian installed, but the machine still froze on boot without ever getting into the desktop environment.

So I tried installing Ubuntu, which, along with Red Hat, was specifically mentioned as now being supported by Lenovo. Success. Installation went smoothly. I was still using the dongle for wifi, so I shut down the machine and reinstalled the inboard card. Again, success. Wifi operated right away.

The couple of minor -- emphasizing minor -- things I don't like is that an inboard white LED glows continually when the power supply is plugged in, and as far as I can tell there's no way to turn it off.

Bottom line here is I think it's a good machine for general use. It's pretty capable, but be aware of its limitations so you won't be disappointed.
text_fidelity_b: Lenovo IdeaCentre 3 Desktop Tower, AMD Athlon Silver 3050U, AMD Radeon Graphics, 4GB DDR4, 256GB SSD, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, HDMI, Windows 10

Canon EF 100mm f/2.8 Macro USM Fixed Lens for Canon SLR Cameras Although this lens is intended for macro photography, it's also a great lens for general purpose shots, or portrait shots. The lens produces beautiful sharp images and is a fast, accurate focuser. The lens is moderately heavy and bulky, so I wouldn't classify it as eminently carryable, and without image stabilization, you might suffer hand shake blur if you're not shooting at the wide end; at smaller apertures, using it with a tripod is highly recommended. But if you're buying it primarily to get into macro this shouldn't much matter as tripod shooting with macro is virtually a necessity, and completely expected.

The 100mm focal length is a nice compromise when you want to get close to small subjects (particularly insects) but are limited to how close you can get before scaring the subject off - as a comparison with the 180mm macro, you would want to factor in a consideration as to what you might like to shoot most of the time - big spiders that you'd rather stay well away from might be an application more suited to the 180mm, for instance, but if you are keen to shoot mostly flowers, the 180 might be more length than you really need.

In short, the 100mm macro is one of my "keeper" lenses, a real performer.
text_fidelity_b: Canon EF 100mm f/2.8 Macro USM Fixed Lens for Canon SLR Cameras

Perixx Peripro-303MR Trackball, 1.34 Inch Replacement Ball for Perimice and M570, Matte Red I bought this replacement ball for my Logitech MX ERGO, which worked well for me before I accidentally dropped it and subsequently put a pock mark on the original ball. The ERGO still worked but would occasionally get stuck when the support pegs would catch the pock and cause the ball to resist - not enough to really hurt anything but just enough to make digital drawing difficult and just enough to annoy me. This replacement ball has taken care of that for me and has proven to be a worthwhile expense for me.

The ERGO and the M570 have the same size ball, so this ball can be used in either (I was using the ball from my old M570 in the ERGO while I waited for this ball to arrive). Replacement is a 30-second procedure and requires no special tools, though a pencil does make getting the old ball out a lot easier.

There are two different finish types available, glossy and matte. I chose the glossy in red. Operation has been absolutely smooth with no resistance at all and no catches. I haven’t noticed any operational differences between it and the original gray ball that came in my ERGO. And, in my opinion, the dark red of this ball actually looks a little nicer than the original silver ball as well as the blue M570 ball.

This wasn’t an expensive replacement and so far it has worked out very well for me. It has restored operation of my trackball to what it was before I damaged the original ball, which is really all I needed. Based on my experience with it, this is an easy replacement ball to recommend if you need to replace the ball in either a Logitech M570 or an MX ERGO.
text_fidelity_b: Perixx Peripro-303MR Trackball, 1.34 Inch Replacement Ball for Perimice and M570, Matte Red

My husband bought me a Kindle and this cover for Christmas and I am in love with both. The case is obviously well made throughout. The leather and binding are solid. The material on the inside covers is lovely to the touch and, not being slick, it offers a little resistance to slipping if you are resting it on another cloth-covered surface like an overstuffed chair arm.

I often read in bed in the dark and love the way the cover works here. At some angles there's a bit of a flare of light on the screen closest to the light, but a little adjustment fixes that. It's tens times easier than wrestling with a paperbound book and an attached book light.

I find that I take my Kindle out of the cover fairly often to play games or do anything much with the key pad. The first day or so I scared myself by not lining it up quite properly and having the top hinge engaged while the bottom one was only part of the way hooked in. I just patiently and gently worked it till the top hinge disengaged and made a mental note to pay a little attention when I slip the Kindle onto the hinges.

Great product.

I suppose the Fm and MW were ok although i didn't spend much time trying them, my goal was to buy a good, "hot' portable SW. This one isn't it...perhaps the luck of the draw with some little discreet component or the factory adjustment as it left the shop. Who knows.

Besides that, there is no AC power pack and you will be finding one to pay for extra. The controls are strange, badly laid out and for some things require both hands on the radio to accomplish. Tiny little switches you cannot see without good light on the end almost guarantee your other fingers will hit the 3 button on the front. More controls on the left end....more controls on the front, many with at least two functions per button. And, the slight but noticeable delay between pushing the up or down frequency button and when it really locks on and you get sound again

Had this radio been really sensitive and really pulled in the distant stations or really done a great job on SW-SSB i would have forced myself to deal with the controls. So, i sent it back. Amazon was great and took it with my description of the problems. Perhaps they have taken some back before. SONY...ARE YOU LISTENING??

text_fidelity_a:
Victrola Retro Wood Bluetooth FM/AM Radio with Rotary Dial, Espresso If you're looking for an inexpensive but very good radio \Bluetooth speaker, this is it. The sound quality isn't perfect but it's very good. If you're looking for speakers for dubstep or heavy bass, you'll need to spend more but it does have good bass for everything else. Additionally, the bass level is adjustable with the tone knob. It's loud, not house rocking loud, but loud enough to hear well outdoors from my living room.
I was surprised to see that this is not rechargeable but connects to the wall, so, not portable. This, however, was exactly what I wanted because every BT speaker I've had breaks down at the charger port. I bought and returned the SEVIZ "40 watt" (actually 4 ten watt speakers) in less than a month for exactly that reason.
I'm not surprised by all the complaints about the radio adjustment given that we live in a time that people have gotten used to everything being automatic, but if you're old enough to know how to use a radio like one from the 80s on back, it's not a problem. It is, after all, a "vintage", non digital, speaker. If you want more precise radio adjustment, buy one with digital tuning.
I get so many stations it's ridiculous and I live at 6000 feet, rural, at least a half hour away from all but two stations, so, if you're not getting stations you must really be in the boonies. I get stations from Mexico and I'm 45 minutes away. The stations also come in very clearly with no interference at all.
I have had a slight issue with the BT competing for a connection with my other speaker and then having a connection with no media or no phone and having to manually reset the connection, but this only happens if both speakers are on.
It's also very solidly built, although, it is manufactured in China. It's MDF, not wood, but it looks great. It's also not one of those vintage speakers you get and end up surprised at how dinky it is and how much it looks like a kid's toy. It's big for a BT speaker.
For the price, this is a great speaker. For the price, you're not getting a Kenwood, an automatic tuner, or tons of bells and whistles. If you want a good speaker for YouTube, TV, or other generalized use, this is it. I definitely recommend it. I'll update if anything untoward happens down the road.
text_fidelity_b: Victrola Retro Wood Bluetooth FM/AM Radio with Rotary Dial, Espresso

Mohu Television Antenna Leaf 30 Paper-Thin Indoor HDTV Antenna for Free TV MH-110502 There are so many good reviews here about this antenna, I'll try not to repeat what others have said. I do have a few tips to add,

When setting up your antenna, do yourself a favor and tie a string through the two holes at the top of the antenna. That way you can hang it on one tack/nail as you're searching for the best location. Have extra tacks or nails handy, as they will jump out of your hand and become lost in the carpet (until you find them the next day with a bare foot).

Buy some very small nails. I've discovered that I need to move the antenna around to get reception for some channels. Therefore I have a fair number of nails in the wall that look a little strange. Small nails are less visually distracting. If I get very ambitious, I might even paint them.

This antenna really works best on an exterior wall facing the majority of transmitting antennas you are trying to reach. So if you're working with an interior wall facing the wrong direction, it probably won't work very well.

To up the number of channels you receive, consider buying a signal amplifier (I bought the RCA Digital Amplifier here on Amazon.) They cost about $15. I added 10 additional channels by using one.

Finally, how well these indoor antennas work largely depends on where you live and how close you are to the transmitting antennas. To avoid disappointment, do some research online before purchasing anything.The site that helped me the most was disablemycable.com .
text_fidelity_b: Mohu Television Antenna Leaf 30 Paper-Thin Indoor HDTV Antenna for Free TV MH-110502

text_fidelity_a:
Display Port to HDMI Converter with Audio Adapter I wanted to hear and see Skype on our Sony XBR7 HDMI-only capable 1080p TV, fed from a Lenovo X220 convertable laptop/tablet running System 7 64 bit Ultimate through the DisplayPort. I also wanted to watch some YouTube videos playing from Firefox and hear their audio on my big living room audio system. No such luck.

When first plugged in, I remember briefly seeing the TV via this DisplayPort adapter in the audio device list, but the next time, the TV disappeared and is nowhere to be found. Not in the audio control panel, anyway. It's just gone.

I first chalked this up to the Thinkpad weirdness, as its internal audio card/mic doesn't work with Skype either. If I plug in an external Logitech webcam, it works seamlessly. Internal camera/mic, nothing.

Sony audio problems aside, the video looks great on the big screen, though it overscans a bit and cuts off part of the menu bar at the bottom.

One reviewer said he could see his TV in the list of audio devices and was able to configure its audio to satisfaction. My Sony TV does not show in the Lenovo audio devices list, though it does show as a generic PnP monitor.

I plugged the HDMI cable into a tiny 7" video monitor and whatdayaknow, the audio came through and the device showed up as an audio device. Then I plugged it into a 20" Vizio and sure enough, it works fine too. Same with a Samsung LCD. Three monitors out of four work. The Sony is the only one that doesn't. Hmmmm.

Sooooo, I'm guessing there's something about Sony's DRM or some other HDMI protocol blocking the computer from seeing the TV. I set all the TVs for internal speakers. Routing audio to an external amp is another variable in the equation.

Nothing wrong with the adapter that I can tell, it simply doesn't see certain Sony TV's.
text_fidelity_b: Display Port to HDMI Converter with Audio Adapter

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech Harmony 900 Rechargeable Remote with Color Touch Screen (Discontinued by Manufacturer) First let me start by saying I am an IT professional and have been a audiophile and video hobbyist for many years. Naturally I have had a lot of different audio / video equipment over the years. I had a computer hooked up to my TV long before it was in fashion. And finally, I am always looking for the next great gadget on the market. Enter the Harmony 900.

Here is my current setup in my living room:
Samsung TV HL-T5687
Sony PS3 Move
Nyko IR Adaptor for PS3 - Media Hub Slim
Roku2 XS
Onkyo TX-NR808
Sharp DVDR-VCR DV-RW340
Cable Box Motorola DVR DCH-3416
Shuttle PC with Media Center
X10 Home Automation - Various Devices

I basically use my TV as a monitor, the only cable plugged into it is the HDMI from the receiver. Hence, the Onkyo receiver does all the sound and switching between inputs.

The Harmony 900 Experience:

I did a lot of research before buying this $250.00 remote. Considering this thing is 50.00 more that my Kindle Fire and does a whole lot less, it wasn't easy pulling the trigger.

Ergonomics:
I read the good and bad reviews and decided that this one would best fit my needs. From many of the negative reviews I concluded the biggest concern was going to be dropping it and breaking the screen. It becomes very obvious why this is the minute you put it in your hand. It is very sleek and conforms well to your hand, but is as a slippery as a fresh water eel in your hand. Also due to the few contact points with any surface other than the charger, it is very easy to slide off a couch arm or get bumped off a coffee table.

That being said, the remote is very well balanced and fits nicely in the hand. The buttons are raised and easy to push. However some of the buttons are simply in the wrong spot. The volume and channel buttons should be reversed and the "Menu" button should be located down further on the remote. The fast forward and skip buttons are perfectly positioned and the skip buttons have a notable bump on them to differentiate between the two.

The screen is actually better than I thought it would be. I can make out the display with or without my (fulltime) glasses. On the down side, it is very easy to tap on the wrong display icon when moving left and right through the screens. When this happens, depending on what you accidentally pressed, it takes a while to recover and get back to what you were watching. Some things may have turned on or off and if you weren't pointing in the right direction during the errant tap, good luck getting everything synced again.

Device Support:

The Harmony 900 claims thousands of supported devices. But good luck finding some of them. Instead of having a simple model number look up, you first have to choose the type of type of device, then the manufacturer followed by the model number. The problem is some devices are not listed in the device type or seem to be randomly added to device types you would not expect them in. There is an example in the set section below.

One thing clearly missing is a simple list of all the devices. In some cases like the X-10 IR interface module listed in many of these reviews, it is no longer available. It would be great to just enter X-10 and see every device that was compatible so you could buy the right one as an interface with the Harmony. There is no way to do this. This is a glaring omission that seems very simple to correct. Heck, a downloadable PDF would be better than nothing.

But all that said, I found every device in my house in their database and I had some fairly obscure AV stuff. And as long as the device is IR, you can custom map from any remote to the Harmony, so there really isn't any IR that cant work.

Setup:

Now I wasn't bragging when I said I was an IT professional. I simply mentioned this fact so those who are technically challenged have a baseline to consider when evaluating their ability to use and set up this device. I have built servers, computers, configured high end routers and switches and oversee hundreds of devices in several locations. And it always amazes me when I get a new piece of equipment like this, how frustrated I can get in the first few minutes of using it.

As others have mentioned, you have to install the software and set up an account to use the device. All settings are done interactively and in real time through the internet. If you don't have an internet connection, don't bother with this remote. I did not use the CD but instead downloaded the latest version from the Logitech web site. I also pre downloaded the owners manual several days before the remote arrived and read it cover to cover. So by the time I had it in my hand I was fairly comfortable with how the setup process should work. The software and driver installation was very easy and there were no USB connection problems to the remote. So far painless!

After letting the remote charge for a couple of hours I started through the setup process. I had used my own version of their worksheet and had all the devices written down. The first thing to note, again as other have mentioned is the Sony PS3 requires an add-on device to translate the IR to the Sony's native RF. Although Logitech sells such a device for almost 100.00, I already had a Nyko Media Hub for the PS3. It doesn't have all the functions of the Logitech, but it was only $17.00 and does all I need. And best of all, the Harmony 900 has the Nyko in it's database. The Roku2 XS is mysteriously placed in the DVD section and if I hadn't read some of these reviews I would not have known that. All the other devices mentioned above were in the database and all were added without an issue.

Once all the devices were added the software prompts you to add activities. Activities are the heart of the 900's functionality. However you must understand the concept of "Activities" and how they work to really get the most out of this remote. In a nutshell, an Activity is started by pressing a single button or in this case an icon like "Watch TV" . When you press Watch TV, the TV turns on and switches to the proper input, the Cable box turns on, the receiver turns on and switches to the proper input and output, and finally the 900 becomes a remote for all of those devices at the same time. More on this later.

To get a feel for this device I decided I would first set up all my devices without any activities. Essentially I wanted to just have a remote and be ability to go to one device after the other and see if they worked correctly. At first the software stumped me and didn't appear to let me get past setting up activities. I gave up trying and set some of them up thinking I could always wipe the remote clean and start again. I am not sure where I went wrong but the first activity I set up, "Watch TV" didn't work out so well. The TV didn't turn on, the Cable box turned off, etc. I ran back and forth from my PC to the living room about a dozen times and finally gave up for the night after about 2 hours of head banging. That night I re-read the manual, had the whole next day to ponder and went at it again .

The next morning I deleted all the activities and created them on my own, not using the wizard. I created an Activity, added the devices and then one by one told the software what I wanted each device to do. This was very helpful. I realized this not only got me the expected result, but it made me see how this software and remote really worked. After playing around for about 30 minutes I was able to create several of my most frequent activates. Going back to the equipment I pressed Watch TV. Again the TV did not turn on. If I used the Harmony for that device directly it worked. Back to the PC and set the activity to turn on the TV first. Still no luck. Next I tried the activity and used the on screen help. It asked if the TV turned on, I answered no and presto the TV turned on. After selects "this fixed my problem" on the remote, it worked every time. But; after each change on the PC I had to go through this help processes. I still do not know what the Harmony is doing to correct this.

Once I got all the basic Activities working I found a few other glitches. When I wanted to watch my combo DVF/VCR and use the VCR portion, none of the commands worked. It turns out this device has separate and distinct commands for FF-VCR and FF-DVD. The Harmony set all the DVD commands to that Activity by Default. I simply created two activities, One Watch VHS and one watch DVD even though it's the same source. In fact I found creating different activities for the same source is the answer to everyone complaining about missing the macro feature. It really does the same thing.

Now that I was on a roll my last bit of programming was renaming the activities. If you want the rest of your family to know how to use this thing without a PowerPoint presentation and tutor, I suggest you name the activities in such a way that its very obvious. Examples are Watch TV, Watch Netflix, Use PC, Listen to iPod, Listen to Pandora, etc. Since my receiver has an iPod dock, the Listen to iPod activity changed the source from whatever it is on to the receivers iPod port and then shows all the different music listening modes on the soft buttons. Watch Netflix switches to my Roku, etc.

Now for the best part of the Harmony setup! Its the ability to have the remote on the "Watch TV" activity and being able to program the hard and soft buttons to any other device's remote function. No more switching to the specific device's remote to change an often used setting on that device. If you take your time, you will eventually never have to use the "Devices" soft button as all the things you do will be setup in the Activity you are in. Now this takes some time and trial and error, but it's a huge time saver. Here is an example: You are Watching TV, controlling the sound options and volume with the Receiver, changing channels with the DVR and changing the aspect ration with the TV all on the same keypad. But beware! You can set what buttons do what on the device settings, but that won't change what they do in an Activity. The remote buttons MUST be set up in the Activity to work properly.

I spent several more days fine tuning the remote and now have not touched it in a while. I have a few more tweaks I am thinking of doing. And I would love to find the glitch that makes the TV turn on after I make any updates to the remote. Maybe a call is in order before my 90 days runs out.

USE:

As mentioned above, the ability to have the most common functions for several devices on one remote mode at the same time is huge! Now that I have used it for a couple of weeks, I have gotten accustomed to the button layout and can operate it without looking at it for most basic functions.

When everything is off and you select Watch TV, everything turns on and goes to the right inputs etc. However starting an activity can take quite a while. The remote can not be used while the Activity is being implemented. In my case I am already watching TV with sound on and the remote is still spinning the hour glass for a while. If you have the TV on too loud, you have to wait until the Harmony is done thinking or walk over and turn it down manually. However once that first activity is complete, any subsequent activity is changed fairly quick.

The battery life seems a bit short. I used to change the batteries in my remote once a year. This thing needs to be charged almost every day. If you let it go dead, its time to break out the old remotes during a recharge.

Once set up properly the Harmony 900 is very easy to use and the rest of the family had no problems with it, well almost.

Wife Problems:If your wife, child, etc. has a habit of turning the TV and other equipment on and off manually, you are in for some headaches. Since the Harmony remembers the last state of your devices (if you use it exclusively), it may turn things on instead of off, or off instead of on if someone else manually did that. My wife figured out the remote very quickly they way I have it set up. But she still does a mixture of using the remote and manual power buttons which frustrates both of us. Of course she blames the remote for not working properly when this happens. However anything that takes some blame from me is more than welcome.

RF Setup:

One of my misconceptions about this remote was the boasting of RF (Radio Frequency) capability. IT does indeed have IR capability. However, it does not have a database of RF codes like it does for IR codes. This device will not replace "ANY" RF remote, period. I was hoping there was a RF option for my X-10 home control devices, but that is not the case. For setups like this you need to get a IR to RF converted for the devices you already have. Figuring out which one you need can be a daunting task (See Device Support above).

The only RF device the Harmony will control directly is the IR blaster that comes with the device. An additional IR blaster can also be added. By default the IR blaster emits all the signals the remote puts out through IR to any and all blasters you have set up. You can control which blaster gets which signal. But this can only be done at the remote, not in the software. I am not sure why this is, but it is one of several deficiencies in the software.

Overall:

I went from wanting to return the Harmony 900 within hours of taking it out of the box, to protecting it like it is one of my children. I really love the Harmony 900 and would recommend it to most people. Those with little patients or difficulty working the microwave should avoid it unless someone else can set it up for you. It's overkill on a simply setup, like DVR and TV. But it is a pure joy if you have a medium to complex setup like I do. At $250.00 it is very pricy and hard to justify for a remote. But it seems to solve all my remote issues and to me it's worth it. I give it 4 stars.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech Harmony 900 Rechargeable Remote with Color Touch Screen (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech Harmony 650 Infrared All in One Remote Control, Universal Remote Logitech, Programmable Remote (Silver) What can I say that hasn't been said by 6,200 previous buyers except that this Harmony 650 in silver is a great remote for a small single-remote system.

I'm using it on a patio with a TiVo, a Vizio 40" and an Amazon Basics SB20 sound bar. All three devices were easily found in the Harmony database and entered effortlessly into the remote using the MyHarmony app you download from Logitech to your laptop or desktop computer.

Having used the MyHarmony app to integrate my two Harmony Ultimate hubs for more complex remote IR systems that employ my network/router/phone as interfaces, I was already familiar with how Logitech has set up their software -- so it took only minutes to get the 650 into action.

Hint: before beginning to program your remote, gather the manufacturer and exact model number for each device you are going to control: TV, Amp, Sound Bar, Cable box, DVD player, Blu-ray Player, CD player, whatever. The MyHarmony software will ask you to add all the devices you are going to integrate. You'll need information from as many devices as you have current remotes for. When you're done, you put all the remotes away and use just the 650.

According to the MyHarmony app, the 650 can control 8 devices. I only needed to control three for my patio setup, so it was a simple process.

Bottom line, it's WAY easier to use a single Harmony 650 that to juggle three remotes (TiVo, Sound Bar and TV).

And after just a few minutes of easy online programming that then downloads to the 650 via a USB cable, I'm done.

As the 650 is being used on the patio outdoors, and subject to environmental attack from dust and moisture, I ordered the silicone cover for it. Works great: [[ASIN:B01N2SF2XX Harmony 650 Silicone Case for Logitech Harmony 650 700 Remote Controller Cover Anti Dust Anti-Slip]]

2 Pack USB Wall Charger Surge Protector, 5 Outlet Extender with 4 USB Charging Ports (1 USB C Outlet) 3 Sided 1800J Power Strip Multi Plug Outlets, Wall Adapter Spaced for Home Office, Black THE GOOD:
--------------
* You get two outlet units in this package.
* The outlets are nicely placed so all my little bricks fit. Do not overlook spacing of outlets, they absolutely matter for an efficient design.
* Three 2.4A USB ports.
* One 3.0A USB-C port.

THE BAD:
------------
* When I saw the stock photos, I thought the middle dot was the screw location. As it turns out, it's just a led light to show you're protected. So the only downside to this design is that you cannot screw in the unit to the wall. I have several Belkin outlets similar to this and they placed the led lights at a different location, so that the middle is dedicated for a long machine screw. We installed this Addtam unit under an entryway table. We store things under this desk, so we'll have to be careful. Also, without the machine screw securing the outlet in place, when you unplug individual plugs or adapters, you'll need to be careful you don't pull the entire unit out the wall. That could happen with tight fighting plugs. So one hand should hold the unit in place, while the other hand unplugs.

I'll go 4-Stars. It would be 5 if they didn't omit the screw slot.

1080P CAM/16GB SD CRD BLK It's always a good thing to be able to monitor your home and your pets while you're away.
Having this EZVIZ video camera, it can't get any easier.

Have been using a different video device for the past year. So wanted to see how this one compared.
Very easy set up. Using the quick set up guide, can have this up and running within a few minutes including downloading the needed app.
Long power cord with this. Can easily plug it in and have enough cord for it to reach a much higher level. Right now I have mine on a small shelf on the wall. If I choose to run it to the ceiling, (sticky pad included to do this) I will definitely get a nice cord cover to hide the cord that would be hanging down the wall to the outlet.

Video quality is really nice and clear. And love the wide angle with this. I can actually see the entire room.
Because I have animals, I have decided not to activate the motion detection. I really don't need alerts, to my phone, every time a dog moves around.
It's nice that I can buy a larger SD memory card for this. I will probably just increase it to 64GB. I really don't want to pay for cloud service so opted out of buying that.
No updates yet so not sure how well the "one-click updates" will work. But, if it works, it will be fantastic adding new features and functionality with just one click.
This is my first EZVIZ security camera but will love letting me see all of my EZVIZ cameras in one place if I choose to buy some more.

Great video security camera, for a decent price, that will definitely get used a LOT.
Would love to expand and eventually have my whole house monitored.

My brother has the largest Kindle Fire HD and it looked very nice. I paid extra to get rid of the ads because they were too obtrusive. One would pop in while I was doing something and shut down that app. I wanted a device for reading e-books and listening to audio books. The app saves to the external storage card but the downloaded content goes directly to the device storage which makes no sense. Why have an external storage option when none of the larger content files will save to it? The sound is more treble than bass, but it sounds good. My device is only 8 GB, so it max'ed out quickly when I downloaded content. I like the thin form factor. This cuts down the amount of weight in my bag. I got the magenta with a purple cover. Maybe it is because this is the first time I am using it, but the OS is very jumpy and the screen is not as responsive as I would like. I have to tap several times to open an app or play a song. Once I figured it out, downloading from my accounts was easy. Unfortunately when I tried to view my internal content, the device went into a loop, then restarted itself and that took a long time. If I ever am able to download to my SD card as the instructions say, then I will be happy to upgrade my review. In the meantime, I am disappointed that this is not able to do what I wanted.

HomeScreen (3 Minute Setup) Touchscreen Dual Band Wireless Router/Range Extender AC750 (802.11ac) I received this as a review sample and even though I am experienced with setting up and configuring networks, this was so easy that I honestly believe anyone can set it up with the scant instructions.

My initial set up was to connect it to my DSL modem just to check it out. Although the instructions are terse, you do need to read them regardless of level of experience. For one thing, it requires you to completely power off your broadband modem. For another, it takes a bit to boot up no matter how you intend to use it. Connecting to broadband was a snap.

What I really wanted was a range extender and this was as simple to configure for that as it was to configure for broadband. In that mode, when you first power it on and boot up it takes over a minute and you may be tempted to think it's broken. Don't. Once it is powered up, like the broadband set up (DSL or cable), the wizard makes it simple to discover your wireless router, connect to it and extend the range of your network. My wireless router turns in a weak -70dB from my master bedroom (measured with [[ASIN:B004EBZX6W Wi-Fi Analyzer]]) and once I installed this in the same room the signal dramatically improved to a strong -40dB. In the same room with my master wireless router this comes in at -47dB while the master router measures in at -56dB. That indicates that the signal of this router is exceptionally strong.

There are options for adding sensors for home control. I did not test that set of features because I did not receive sensors, but it is functionality that makes this router/extender a great choice if you do want to pursue home control too. There are IOS and Android apps that can be used in conjunction with the sensor features. Again, I did not explore those and probably will not since I am not interested in them. As a router alone I love this, and especially the overall signal strength and ease of setting up and configuring.
text_fidelity_b: HomeScreen (3 Minute Setup) Touchscreen Dual Band Wireless Router/Range Extender AC750 (802.11ac)

My final test was between the Fire and the Samsung Galaxy Tab 7.0. The Fire was faster! The start up time is faster on the Fire than the new iPad...that is not from reboot.

I have had my Kindle Fire for two months now and am still in love. I am particularly enjoying the whole Amazon experience: the free app a day, the free books every day, the lending library with Prime and the free TV and movies with Prime, as well. I can not say enough good things about this system.

My husband was so taken with my enjoyment of the Fire that he just bought one himself. He is in love, too! Now I can loan him books. I was going to purchase the new iPad this summer, but now I think I will wait another year. :-)

ASUS ROG GL552VW-DH74 15-Inch Gaming Laptop, Discrete GPU GeForce GTX 960M 4GB VRAM, 16GB DDR4, 1TB, 128GB SSD (ROG Metallic) I knew the keyboard was red when I ordered it. I didn't know how bad that would suck, however. The keys are hard to read during the day. So you have no choice but to crank the backlight to max, wasting battery. Battery life is bad enough as it is. And the backlighting doesn't help much during the day. I just hate it.

Next issue is that it doesn't come with DVD playing software. Seriously? Why did I buy a computer with a DVD player in it? Asus support informs me that I should buy a third party DVD playing app as Microsoft won't let them include it. Really. I ended up researching and finding VLC player but come on. My Toshiba windows 10 laptop came with DVD playing software and it doesn't even HAVE a dvd drive!

Finally, I'm very used to having the function keys be utility keys. Brightness, volume, etc. And I like it that way. I don't use the F functions often (F11 is about the only one) and prefer to use the fn key for them when I do. Asus is set up to do the opposite. Most other manufacturers give you a way to reverse that behavior. EIther a fn lock key or a bios setting or something. Not Asus. Nope, you're stuck with it the way they like it.

Unfortunately I'm stuck with this laptop since Amazon has a lousy return policy on computers. Maybe some 13 year old will think it's cool and want to buy it. I hope so.
text_fidelity_b: ASUS ROG GL552VW-DH74 15-Inch Gaming Laptop, Discrete GPU GeForce GTX 960M 4GB VRAM, 16GB DDR4, 1TB, 128GB SSD (ROG Metallic)

text_fidelity_a:
Garmin 4.3-Inch Carrying Case Bought this for the 750 because it didn't come with a case. A similar (smaller) case came with my 360 and I didn't think this purchase through. After using it and comparing the other cases out there, I would buy a different case.

This slipcase for the 750 fits tight. That's good. The Nuvi won't slip out. But because the 750's on/off switch is now a slider on the top left corner, if you slide it into the case naturally (unit in your right hand, case in your left) the switch rubs against the case. When you pull the unit out, it "automatically" turns on. Thus if you were to pull the unit out partially then push it back in, you could turn it on and not know it.

The solution is to invert the Nuvi so its switch will be at the open end of the case after it's in the case. That way you can see the switch's on/off position and verify it's not on.

More practical issues:

Pros:

- Nicely made: very high quality

- Very compact

- Adequate protection against rattling inside a glove compartment or briefcase

- Good basic case

Cons:

- It can accidentally turn the unit on

- It's black: can't find it easily in the dark buried at the bottom of my shoulder bag when traveling. Experienced this with the 360's case. And if it falls on the floor of a rental car at night, good luck trying to find it. Wish it came in natural leather color.

- Offers no protection while hand holding the unit while walking

The [[ASIN:B0012MI7N2 Garmin Nuvi 800 Series Carrying Case]] case is a wallet style that flips open to reveal the screen. text_fidelity_a:
Brainwavz R3 Dual Dynamic Driver Earphones (V2) Prior to receiving this review sample I was happy with in-ear type phones, but always grabbed headphones when I wanted to listen to music without disturbing others, These phones changed that. For one thing they are super comfortable. For another the sound is incredible. In fact I have been testing various phones - mainly from this brand, but also some Sennheiser models - and this is head and shoulders above the pack.

I'll be honest and disclose that comfort edges out sound when phones sound good enough. I will normally not quibble over a few hundred Hz one way or the other as long as I can wear the phones without noticing them. These are not only unobtrusive, but downright comfortable, which is a major reason why these have now replaced my trusty [[ASIN:B00ENZRS76 Brainwavz HM9 Hi-Fi Noise Isolating Headphones]].

Soundwise the specs do not begin to describe the richness, especially bass. In fact, when I read the 20 Hz to 20 MHz range I thought that the sound would be somewhat generic for phones in this range. I own a pair of IEMs (in-ear monitors) that go as low as 18 Hz at the same 95dB at 1mW sensitivity, yet these sound much deeper than those. I love the balance of sound across the frequency spectrum as though it's on a smooth continuum. Every one of my test albums I played through these phones sounded so good that I decided that it's time to hang up the headphones and go with these.

Part of the reason why I love these from a comfort perspective is the over the ear memory wire. I prefer that style, but not everyone does. They are definitely stiff and take on a shape that will be uniquely yours over time (and a very short time at that!) Also, while this ships with a [[ASIN:B00HPPL1M4 Brainwavz Hard Earphone Case]] the phones will not fit after you have contoured them to your ear. The case is useful for carrying around the array of adapters and tips that are included. In fact, the final reason I love these phones is the included triple-flange style silicon tips, which block out the rest of the world and allow me to focus solely on music.

If you love music and want to hear every note faithfully reproduced in their natural frequencies these phones are it. I can honestly say that I have not used a better set of phones from any brand in this price range, including some Sennheiser models that have a street price of fifty to seventy-five dollars more than these, so the value is definitely there.
text_fidelity_b: Brainwavz R3 Dual Dynamic Driver Earphones (V2)

Belkin Verve Folio Case with Stand for Samsung Galaxy Tab 10.1inch (Black) My favorite types of cases are the rigid style that grab onto the edges of the device and do not increase the width or length of the device significantly. This is sort of a hybrid between that style and Belkin's ultrathin folio style.

That's because this one has a "pocket" for the device just like the soft ultrathins, which means you see the screen through a well placed cutout. It also has holes cut for the buttons, lenses, and ports. It is smaller from a length and width perspective than the ultrathin, but a bit deeper because the cover is thicker. It also has cleaner lines, although not as clean as some hard cases.

It also has an elastic strap attached to the cover that can be turned around to hold the case shut. Only time will tell if that stays nice and tight or ends up sagging after use. Really, it doesn't need to be used often as the case will mostly stay shut by itself.

The one thing I don't like is the way you fold the front cover behind the back: it sort of seems too stiff, as if you're not really supposed to. It also folds at both joints, which keeps it from lying completely flat. The ultrathin folio has it beat in that case, although I like the Verve in better in most other ways.

A nice case for your tablet.
text_fidelity_b: Belkin Verve Folio Case with Stand for Samsung Galaxy Tab 10.1inch (Black)

text_fidelity_a: Blink XT Home Security Camera System - 5 Camera Kit - 1st Gen I tried to love these cameras but they've let me down several times now.  Their motion detection is erratic at the best of times and since there's no ability to continuously record to an sd card or anything else, if the the motion detector doesn't catch it, it's not recorded. It takes too long for the cameras to wake up so I get a lot of 'blank' clips, where whatever finally triggered the camera is over by the time it gets around to recording it. Worst of all, the whole system has a tendency to randomly go offline where it stops communicating with the cameras and nothing gets recorded. After the neighbors annoying free-roaming dogs set off my Wyze cam for the 20th time today it suddenly occurred to me to wonder why I wasn't getting Blink alerts. So I checked, and lo and behold, I wasn't able to connect to any of the cameras, and apparently hadn't been connected for at least 18 hrs based on the last stored clips. But there's no indication of any problem on the aggravatingly bright leds on the hub, they look like everything is peachy. I had to unplug the hub for a few minuted then reconnect. Not so convenient when you're not home, which is when you most definitely want your cameras to work. This is the second time this has happened and I'm done. Returning these.

text_fidelity_a:
StarTech.com Dual Monitor USB 3.0 Laptop Docking Station with HDMI & DVI/VGA, 6x USB-A Hub, GbE, Audio, Universal Type-A Dock - Windows/macOS/ChromeOS (USB3SDOCKHD) I had high hopes for this docking station from StarTech but, thus far, I’ve been pretty disappointed.

Like many people I like the portability of working from a laptop but when I am at my workstation I want more screen space to work on - I thought this Docking Station would be a perfect solution. Well, in theory, it would.

Inside the box you’ll find the docking station, a 3.0 USB cable, a power adapter with snap on plugs to fit various world power sources, a DVI to VGA adapter, and a CD-ROM.

Unlike many docking stations or hubs this is not Plug and Play. I’m running the most updated Windows 10 64bit and the CD-ROM is completely useless. After inserting it in my computer I received a message reading that it was not compatible with my machine. No problem, I went to the manufacturer’s website, found the product, clicked on support, downloaded the zip file containing the setup and updated drivers for my OS and continued.

I went through the installation process and it appeared to install fine. After accepting the user agreement it checked my system for compatibility - finding no issues it continued and completed installation. I went to device manager and noticed an error in USB connected devices but figured with a restart it would correct.

I restarted but the error remains. Configuration Descriptor Request Failed - Windows has stopped device. I have uninstalled and reinstalled, searched help, used Windows Update to search for a better driver - so far nothing has worked.

In regards to functionality - the USB ports (two 3.0 and four 2.0) all function without issue and the Ethernet Port works great providing me over 200Mb/s. Due to not having the correct drivers I’ve been unable to test the multiple monitor capabilities.

I have contacted tech support and as of writing I have not heard back. If they are able to help me solve these issues I will update my review to reflect my further findings.

It appears this Docking Station is outdated being developed for older operating systems and while it may work for some users, others will find it needlessly difficult.

I would look at more recently manufactured docking stations that have been developed with the current operating systems - especially if you are using Windows 10.
text_fidelity_b: StarTech.com Dual Monitor USB 3.0 Laptop Docking Station with HDMI & DVI/VGA, 6x USB-A Hub, GbE, Audio, Universal Type-A Dock - Windows/macOS/ChromeOS (USB3SDOCKHD)

MOSISO Fashion Laptop Backpack for Women, Pure Deep Gray I am in love with this bag!
It has so many features that are important to me.
I plan on using this bag for day trips with the family and especially during my childrens' swim meets.
This bag has more compartments and zippers then I expected it to have.
There are three main large compartments, two small compartments in the front and an anti-theft pocket in the back and the side water bottle mesh are also contained in a pocket. I was a little worried that I wouldn't be able to fit my water bottle in the outside mesh since there is a zipper and extra fabric and stuff, but as you can see from my image, a sports drink bottle fits perfectly in there.
The bag comes with its own lock which can be programmed to your own code.
The bag has two padded sections within the two largest zippered areas. One for a laptop with a velcro strip and one in the middle section with no velcro.
I plan to use the middle padded area for my mp3 player as this is the area that the headphone cables enter into and I will also put my power bank in that padded area since this is also where the charger port comes from.
The color of this bag is very modern, it's a good bag for a male or female.
I like that I can zip shut the drink compartments if I wanted to have something in them that I don't want to fall out (skittles/sunflower seeds)!
There is a padded carry handle and a non-padded hanging handle which is really nice. The back is very padded as are the shoulder straps.
There is even a luggage strap for if I wanted to bring this on the plane trip.
There are two cinch straps above each water bottle which is nice, as sometimes I like to cinch in my jacket or if I had a lot of bulky stuff inside that could be cinched to remove air and the bulk.
The bag has the interior organization in the front large compartment, including a clip for your keys, two wider sections, mesh on one and two pencil holes, which is great for me as I like to bring a pencil, sharpie, and highlighter with me to the swim meets.
I like that there are so many large compartments, allowing me to keep my stuff separate. I like to bring magazines to read between heats and sometimes my laptop (rear), snacks in the middle and the schedule and journal in the front.
I like the smaller compartment to contain the emergency kit (bandaids, pain reliever, etc).
I don't think there is anything else in a bag that this bag doesn't have.
A great mom bag!
