text_fidelity_a:
Outdoor WiFi Security Camera, HD 1080P Wireless Survenience IP Camera with 32GB SD Card, IP66 Waterproof Bullet Camera for Home, Support Motion Detection FTP 65ft Night Vision Remote View Onvif Cam [[VIDEOID:bcc01f35bd32d1e66d3df81c3dace063]] Updated as promised: After working with the company I was able to completely secure the camera and still access it remotely. After all the initial problems and concerns I have had it installed and working for about a month I guess. It's working great on a variety of different software and protocols. I even tried connecting it to the Angelcam website and using DDNS. Works great with just about everything. With the 128GB SD card it does great. I uploaded some new photos of it working and the different clients being used securely. This turned out to be a great buy because the image quality is incredible and it's got an incredibly wide angle.

You cannot see the IR light like that at night it's only because of the camera I used you can see it. I did that for a reason so that everyone could see the amount of IR light it puts out. The infrared works great as you can see but the motion sensor even on the least sensitive setting picks up rains and bugs flying in front of it. Almost all motion sensors do. The audio sensor works great but the alarm feature doesn't because it's only one way audio. The email was easy to setup once you know which smtp server your ISP uses which WOW doesn't like giving theirs out even to paying customers. The video was provided by them and helped a lot because the screws were impossible to see and there are unnecessary ones in there that don't need to be removed. I have posted the material they sent me as well. I hope this helps everyone out.

BEFORE EDIT AND CUSTOMER SUPPORT:
So far I have had a lot of issues with this camera and still haven't got it to where I would trust letting it outside my isolated LAN which mean I cannot view remotely as of yet. I changed the 32Gb SD card out to a 128Gb card after contacting support since there is no instructions online or anywhere else on how to do it. Turns out it's the one tiny screw in on the top to remove the black piece and then you must carefully unscrew the lens cap. After that you will find several screws lowered besides the lens and IR area. You only need to remove the 4 of the screws. If you look really close with magnification you can see exactly what screws you need to remove because you can see how they hold the board underneath in place. Underneath the lens is the board that holds the SD-Card. Their support was nice enough to send me a video later on. I plan on posting that later after I get this all working. As of now it is telling me I need to reset the camera and there is no reset button that I can find. I am guessing it must be on that board again which means I am going to have to pull the whole thing apart again. In my opinion this is very poorly designed and not very good for people who like to customize or configure their devices. I do not like the way the it acts as soon as it connects to your network. I am still working on testing and hope I can get these issues resolved soon. The picture quality is great but there is a serious lack of security and other major issues plaguing this device. I am going to do some further testing and contact support once again about resetting this camera hopefully without having to dissemble it again but I don't see how. It has been disconnected for hours without power and will not reset that way. I also notice that the camera unit get's extremely hot for some reason. This will defiantly shorten it's life span. More to come on this product but for now I do not recommend buying this unless you are familiar with IP camera installation, network configuration, and have some electrical experience as far as handling circuit boards. This has been a real pain in the read since day one but I am hoping it will be worth it but time will tell. I will upload the video provided by them after getting their consent.
text_fidelity_b: Outdoor WiFi Security Camera, HD 1080P Wireless Survenience IP Camera with 32GB SD Card, IP66 Waterproof Bullet Camera for Home, Support Motion Detection FTP 65ft Night Vision Remote View Onvif Cam

Dell Inspiron 14 Plus 7420 Laptop - 14 inch, 2.2K 16:10, Intel Core i7-12700H, 16GB DDR5 RAM, 1TB SSD, Intel Iris Xe, 2 Yr Onsite + AntiVirus, Migrate, Windows 11 Pro+Office 365 - Atlantic Green The Dell Inspiron 14 Plus 7420 Laptop, what a sleek little machine. It has a nice slate grey color with a matte finish. It is thin, it is powerful, and it just fits what my wife uses it for, which is some office work (word, excel, emails) and some media consumption (videos, social media, etc). Pretty much what everyone would need a laptop for.

Unfortunately, I'm unable to test this computer to its fullest with some games or video editing because I haven't been able to pry it away from my wife since she got it.

Looking simply at the specs of this machine, it is obvious that the i7 12th generation with the Intel Iris integrated graphics will be able to handle anything a casual user would be able to throw at it. The 16gb of ram will handle a LOT of browser windows and application being open at the same time. The 1tb ssd is actually great to have considering that many laptops only include half of this storage. Lastly, the 2.2K resolution is perfect for this small 14" screen. It's higher than full-hd 1080p and isn't too high to where the text and icons are barely legible.

The keyboard is the standard chiclet keys with good travel. It is quite and works well enough to not cause typos or missed key presses.

The screen is comfortable to look at and at 14" it allows this laptop to be a great portable workhorse.

Overall, I'm impressed with the stability, comfort, and just the build quality of this product. With the powerful CPU, I expect that this machine can last for quite a few years.

text_fidelity_a:
NVIDIA Shield TV | 4K HDR Streaming Media Player The world's first all-in-one Plex box, the Shield comes w/ an unlockable (free) Plex Server inside --and not just another client/player like all other consoles. For those of us w/ a LOT of media, Plex is the pinnacle of enjoying your own media with the best interface possible (and it's free); whereas KODI is the best way for streaming media from the internet. The Shield recognized my old archives instantly, and also when I plugged in a USB3 SanDisk flash drive for extra space. I've had 3 WDTVs, 2 Nexus Players, and 1 MiBox, and I wasted all of that time and money until I got this. I've KODI Phoenix and Exodus for internet streaming, and Plex for my 200 movies, 25 seasons of TV shows, 75 instructional videos (on guitar, magic, and yoga), 6k songs, and all my family albums and artwork. I have the Plex client (player) for TV, phones/tablets, XBox 360, Chromebooks, and Chromebox.

The Shield has BOTH the Play Store and the NVidia Store on its dashboard. I can play all my games again because this console doesn't stutter and freeze up. I'd missed my Asphalt 8 when the others just couldn't handle the workload anymore. I can get even better games from the NVidia Store that the Play Sore doesn't have. Of course, all previous purchases come right back to the Shield --like the HomeRun HD. Plex has a deal they're making w/ HomeRun HD to possibly turn the shield into also doing DVR.

The gamepad has been totally redesigned and has gone from an Ugly Duckling to being prettier than a pail full of kittens. The hex-grip feels good in the hand for shooting zombies or driving on racetracks. The gamepad is rechargeable (yay!) and even comes w/ it's own charging cable. The once $50-extra remote is now included w/ the console. Like the gamepad, the remote also has a headphone jack for discreet listening and a touchscreen volume control and Mute.
text_fidelity_b: NVIDIA Shield TV | 4K HDR Streaming Media Player

text_fidelity_a:
SanDisk 32GB Class 4 SDHC Memory Card, Frustration-Free Packaging- SDSDB-032G-AFFP (Label May Change) This review is of the 64GB SDHX card. I use it for a specific purpose: backing up my document folders on my two laptops. It works perfectly with my Windows XP systems over ancient USB 2.0 ports. I can still back up a full card in less than an hour, and if I were on a more modern system with USB 3.0 it would take only a fraction of that time.

This particular card will NOT work in my Samsung Galaxy Note II (I had to try anyway). In fact, make sure your device will actually accept SDHX cards before purchaing this 64GB model or you may be disappointed. Most Microsoft Windows systems running XP service pack 2 or later, Windows CE and Server 2003 will recognize this card, as will Mac OS X Snow Leopard 10.6.5 or later. Phones, tablets and devices running Microsoft Windows RT will also recognize this card. Beyond that check first.

Back to how I use this card: the price for this card is around forty bucks at the time of this review. I could have gotten an exernal hard drive in the terabyte range for twice that, but this has no moving parts, fits in my wallet and with a [[ASIN:B00FSDKBYY Sabrent SuperSpeed USB 3.0 Flash Memory Card Reader]] plugs into any computer (with an operating system that supports the format) via USB ports. For me it's convenient, especially since I am only backing up working documents and never come close to the 64GB capacity (which is closer to 56GB formatted.) In fact I use two of these in rotation for safety, overwriting the older one completely since it takes less than an hour. I always keep the other one on my person.

As the SDHX standard becomes more established and ubiquitous this type of card may work with more devices. At 64GB this is probably the smallest size since the SDHX format was designed to accomodate up to two terabytes. So unless you have a device that is compatible with this format, or you are using it for a single purpose on a supported operating system, you may want to get an SDHC card instead.
text_fidelity_b: SanDisk 32GB Class 4 SDHC Memory Card, Frustration-Free Packaging- SDSDB-032G-AFFP (Label May Change)

text_fidelity_a:
2023 Amplified HD Digital TV Antenna Long 250+ Miles Range - Support 4K 8K 1080p Fire tv Stick and All TV's - Indoor Smart Switch Amplifier Signal Booster - 18ft HDTV Cable/AC Adapters Likes.

Well made.
Long cord. The long cord is very important.

Setup.

I used the long cord to place it on the floor, next to my patio door.
I then set my TV to auto scan.
It gave me many more stations than my non amplified leaf antennae pulled in.
Every station was crystal clear.
However, that was not a convenient permanent location, so I then placed it behind the TV.
It was important to first place it in the best possible area, in my case against the patio door to identify all possible stations.

Issues.

After auto scan identified all possible stations, I moved the antenna to behind my entertainment center. I lost half the stations. But, the TV showed those station numbers, it just couldn't pull them in. I then placed it flat on top of the entertainment center. It improved the reception. I then slid it partially inside my TV wall mount hardware, flat against the wall. It gave me excellent reception on all identified stations.

My advice.

Take advantage of the long cord, move it next to a window even if it won't be left there. You can then place the antenna in more convenient locations, trying to get back to as many identified stations as possible.
text_fidelity_b: 2023 Amplified HD Digital TV Antenna Long 250+ Miles Range - Support 4K 8K 1080p Fire tv Stick and All TV's - Indoor Smart Switch Amplifier Signal Booster - 18ft HDTV Cable/AC Adapters

text_fidelity_a: Fire HD 10 Tablet with Alexa Hands-Free, 10.1" 1080p Full HD Display, 32 GB, Marine Blue (Previous Generation - 7th) Great tablet! I’d compare this more to the Samsung tabs of the 200-300 range and if I’m spending 300 I might as well get the refurb lower end iPad.  This 10.1 Fire tab or iPad, period. Beautiful screen.
